hero.subtitle: The current standard for Internet email delivery, defining how billions of messages are routed and delivered every day.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5321 is the current definitive specification for SMTP, superseding RFC 2821 and the original RFC 821. It describes the protocol for reliable and efficient email transfer.

This RFC defines Extended SMTP (ESMTP), which adds service extension negotiation via the EHLO command, supporting features like TLS, authentication, and pipelining.

sections.title: Mail System Architecture
sections.content:
The SMTP mail system consists of several components:

MUAMail User Agent - the email client (Outlook, Thunderbird, Gmail)
MSAMail Submission Agent - accepts mail from MUAs (port 587)
MTAMail Transfer Agent - relays mail between servers (port 25)
MDAMail Delivery Agent - delivers mail to recipient mailboxes
MX RecordDNS record pointing to the receiving mail server for a domain

sections.title: SMTP Extensions
sections.content:
ESMTP allows servers to advertise supported extensions in response to the EHLO command:

EHLO Capability Advertisement
S: 250-mail.example.com Hello
S: 250-SIZE 35882577
S: 250-8BITMIME
S: 250-STARTTLS
S: 250-AUTH LOGIN PLAIN
S: 250-PIPELINING
S: 250 SMTPUTF8

sections.title: Mail Delivery Process
sections.content:
1. DNS Lookup
Sending MTA queries DNS for the MX records of the recipient's domain
2. Connection
Connect to the highest-priority MX host on port 25
3. EHLO Exchange
Negotiate capabilities, optionally upgrade to TLS
4. Envelope
Send MAIL FROM and RCPT TO commands
5. Message Transfer
Send headers and body via DATA command, terminated by CRLF.CRLF

references.text: Klensin, J., "Simple Mail Transfer Protocol", RFC 5321, October 2008.
Resnick, P., "Internet Message Format", RFC 5322, October 2008.
